<!-- cli-reference:start — generated by `go run ./tools/sitecli` from the CLI; edit the command's help in the code, not this block -->

Declare that a change proves nothing new, keeping the files' evidence fresh.

```text
Moves the evidence of each file to its current content — the tests that proved it, the
stamps and judgments of its edges, what other tests recorded of it — because the change
does not touch what was proven. Anchors cannot tell a trace annotation, a region marker or
a comment from a behaviour change in every language; whoever made the change can, and says
why. The reason is required, and recorded on the file's node.

  anchors keep-evidence a.spec.md b.spec.md --reason "only @realizes added to the rule lines"
  anchors keep-evidence src/Screen.tsx --reason "#region markers around the scenarios" 
  anchors keep-evidence src/pay.ts --lines --reason "a comment on a line of its own was reworded"

Coverage and mutation name lines by number, and an edit that added or removed lines moved
them: they are kept only with --lines, when no line moved. When the map was rebuilt after
the change and no longer holds the evidence, it is taken from the map at HEAD.

The `@contract` stamps of the doubles pointing at the file are refreshed too, and listed.

What proves nothing by itself needs no declaration: the map carries the evidence across a
header's date, a spec's navigation or change history, and the chain's flags (`@dep`,
`@used-by`, `@navigates`). A spec whose rule changed and nothing else keeps its other
proofs, with that rule's scenarios stale; this command keeps those too.

Do not use it for a change in behaviour: the evidence is what stops that change from passing
unproven.
```

## Uso

```bash
anchors keep-evidence <file>... [flags]
```

## Flags

| Flag | Padrão | O que faz |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--lines` |  | also keep coverage and mutation: no line moved |
| `--reason` |  | why the change proves nothing new (required) |
| `--root` | `.` | project root |

## O mapa e seus sinais — família

Comandos da mesma família — o que distingue cada um:

| Comando | O que faz |
| --- | --- |
| [`anchors map`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/map/) | Operate the dependency map (anchors.graph.yaml) |
| [`anchors ingest`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/ingest/) | Ingest test signals (JUnit/lcov) the project generated and bind them to the map |
| [`anchors test`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/test/) | Run the test suites declared in anchors.yaml and ingest the reports |
| [`anchors mutation`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/mutation/) | Run the mutation suites declared in anchors.yaml and ingest the reports |
| **`anchors keep-evidence`** | Declare that a change proves nothing new, keeping the files' evidence fresh |
| [`anchors stamp`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/stamp/) | Write the missing `@contract` stamps on test doubles (never rewrites an existing one) |
| [`anchors recode`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/recode/) | Rename an identity code and propagate it across the project |
| [`anchors renumber`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/renumber/) | Renumber the revisions this branch added when the base already took their number |
| [`anchors generated-paths`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/generated-paths/) | The paths of DERIVED files — whoever conflicts in them rebuilds |
| [`anchors merge-progress`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/merge-progress/) | Progress merge driver: unites both sides, `[x]` beats `[ ]` |
